items.title: Section: The Visible Signs of Anger and Delusion Types

items.zh: 諸根枯槁、諸根剛強、諸根疎澀、諸根麁燥，為性好樂以惡身語損惱於他，易令遠離、易令厭患，兇暴強口、形相稜層，無多勝解，事業不堅、事業不固，禁戒不堅、禁戒不固，不忍不受，多憂多惱，性好違背，所取不順，性多愁慼，性好麁言，多懷嫌恨，意樂慘烈，悖惡尤䖧，好相拒對，得少語言多恚多憤，憔悴而住，喜生忿怒，眉面顰蹙，恒不舒顏，邪精下視，於他榮利多憎多嫉。如是等類，應知是名瞋行者相。問：癡行補特伽羅應知何相？答：癡行補特伽羅，於諸微劣所愚事中，尚能生起最極、厚重、上品癡纏，何況中品、上品境界。又此癡纏住在身中，經久相續，長時隨縛。由此癡纏，為可癡法之所制伏，不能制伏彼可癡法。諸根闇鈍、諸根愚昧、諸根羸劣，身業慢緩、語業慢緩，惡思所思、惡說所說、惡作所作，嬾墮懈怠，起不圓滿，詞辯薄弱，性不聰敏，念多忘失，不正知住，所取左僻，難使遠離、難使厭患，下劣勝解，頑騃、瘖瘂，以手代言，無有力能領解善說、惡說法義，緣所牽纏，他所引奪，他所策使。如是等類，應知是名癡行者相。
items.en: Their faculties are withered, rigid, alienating, and coarse; they are, by nature, prone to harming others through harsh speech and action; they are easily separated from what provokes them and easily brought to disgust with it … given to sudden anger, brow perpetually furrowed, face never open, gaze askance and downwards, deeply envious and resentful of others' honour and gain. All such traits are the marks of an anger-type. … Their faculties are dull, clouded, and feeble; their bodily and verbal actions sluggish; their thoughts, words, and deeds unwholesome; given to laziness and idleness … entangled by circumstance, easily led astray by others, easily ordered about by others. All such traits are the marks of a delusion-type.

items.zh: 問：慢行補特伽羅應知何相？答：慢行補特伽羅，於諸微劣所慢事中，尚能生起最極、厚重、上品慢纏，何況中品、上品境界。又此慢纏住在身中，經久相續，長時隨縛。由慢纏故，為可慢法之所制伏，不能制伏彼可慢法。

items.title: The Visible Signs of the Pride-Type and the Discursive-Thought-Type

items.zh: 諸根掉動、諸根高舉、諸根散亂，勤樂嚴身，言語高大，不樂謙下，於其父母、眷屬、師長不能時時如法承事，多懷憍傲，不能以身禮敬、問訊、合掌、迎逆、修和敬業，自高自舉，陵蔑他人。樂著利養、樂著恭敬、樂著世間稱譽聲頌，所為輕舉，喜作嘲調，難使遠離、難使厭患，廣大勝解，微劣慈悲，計我有情、命者、養者、補特伽羅、生者等見，多分上品，多怨、多恨。如是等類，應知是名慢行者相。問：尋思行補特伽羅應知何相？答：尋思行補特伽羅，於諸微劣所尋思事，尚能發起最極厚重、上品、尋思纏，何況中品、上品境界。此尋思纏住在身中，經久相續，長時隨縛。
items.en: Their faculties are restless, held high, and scattered; they delight in adorning the body, speak loudly and boastfully, and take no pleasure in humility; they cannot regularly attend properly upon their parents, relatives, or teachers, being much given to arrogance … holding views of self, of a sentient being, of a life-principle, of a nourisher, of a person, of one who is born, and the like — mostly of the coarser sort — and harbouring much resentment and hatred. All such traits are the marks of a pride-type. … Answer: A discursive-thought-type practitioner, even towards the most trivial matters, can still generate the most extreme, heavy, superior-grade entanglement of discursive thought — how much more so towards middling or superior matters. This entanglement lodges within them, continuing without break, binding them over a long time.

items.zh: 由此纏故，為可尋思法之所制伏，不能制伏可尋思法。

items.title: Section: Temperament Closes; Vow-Difference Opens — Vows Shift, Lineage Does Not

items.zh: 諸根不住、諸根飄舉、諸根掉動、諸根散亂，身業誤失、語業誤失，難使遠離、難使厭患，喜為戲論、樂著戲論，多惑、多疑、多懷樂欲，禁戒不堅、禁戒不定，事業不堅、事業不定，多懷恐慮，念多忘失，不樂遠離，多樂散動，於諸世間種種妙事貪欲隨流，翹勤無惰，起發圓滿。如是等類，應知是名尋思行者相。如是名為由行差別建立補特伽羅。云何由願差別建立補特伽羅？謂或有補特伽羅於聲聞乘已發正願，或有補特伽羅於獨覺乘已發正願，或有補特伽羅於其大乘已發正願。當知此中，若補特伽羅於聲聞乘已發正願，彼或聲聞種姓，或獨覺種姓，或大乘種姓；若補特伽羅於獨覺菩提已發正願，彼或獨覺種姓，或聲聞種姓，或大乘種姓；若補特伽羅於其大乘已發正願，彼或大乘種姓，或獨覺種姓，或聲聞種姓。若聲聞種姓補特伽羅，於獨覺菩提、或於無上正等菩提已發正願，彼是聲聞種姓故，後時決定還捨彼願，必唯安住聲聞乘願。獨覺乘種姓、大乘種姓補特伽羅，應知亦爾。此中所有補特伽羅，願可移轉、願可捨離，決定不可移轉種姓、捨離種
items.en: Their faculties are unsettled, flighty, agitated, and scattered … much given to confusion, doubt, and restless craving; their discipline unsteady and undecided, their undertakings unsteady and undecided … All such traits are the marks of a discursive-thought-type. How does difference of vow classify practitioners? Some practitioners have formed a genuine vow towards the hearer-disciple vehicle; some towards the solitary-realiser vehicle; some towards the great vehicle. … If a practitioner of the hearer-disciple lineage has formed a genuine vow towards solitary awakening, or towards unsurpassed complete awakening, then, precisely because their lineage is that of a hearer-disciple, they will in time inevitably abandon that vow and settle permanently into the hearer-disciple's vow alone. … Among such practitioners, the vow itself may shift, may be abandoned — but the underlying lineage can never shift, can never be abandoned.

items.zh: 姓。今此義中，當知唯說聲聞乘願、聲聞種姓補特伽羅。如是名為由願差別建立補特伽羅。

blocks.text: How a teacher can recognise a student's temperament from outward signs, and the difference between a vow and a lineage.

"Their faculties are withered, rigid, alienating, and coarse"; they are prone to harsh speech, "brow perpetually furrowed, gaze askance", envious of others' honour. Yet they are "easily separated from what provokes them and easily brought to disgust with it". Master Cháng Bǎi: told that anger is harmful, they turn away from it readily.

"Their faculties are dull, clouded, and feeble; their bodily and verbal actions sluggish"; given to laziness, "easily led astray by others". Venerable Miào Jìng: at root, not believing in dependent origination.

"Their faculties are restless, held high, scattered; they delight in adorning the body, speak loudly and boastfully, take no pleasure in humility; they cannot attend properly upon parents, relatives, teachers." They talk much about self, being, and person.
"Their faculties are unsettled, flighty, agitated"; much given to doubt; their discipline and undertakings "unsteady and undecided".

A person may vow to become a hearer, a solitary buddha, or a bodhisattva. "The vow itself may shift, may be abandoned, but the underlying lineage can never shift." One whose lineage is that of a hearer, even with a bodhisattva vow, "will in time abandon that vow and settle into the hearer path". This is the Yogācāra doctrine of fixed lineages; later East Asian schools disputed it.
The descriptions of temperament are for teachers choosing practices (fascicle 26's next topic). They are useful for self-knowledge too: which of these do I recognise in myself?

quiz.q: The anger-type is "easily separated, easily brought to disgust." How do the masters explain this?
options: Cháng Bǎi: told of anger's faults, they readily turn from the hateful; Miào Jìng: tell them to go and they go easily
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the anger-type easily turns from the hateful; told that anger is bad and faulty, they become averse and turn away. Venerable Miào Jìng: tell this person to leave, and they leave easily.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the delusion-type's "dull faculties"?
options: not believing the Dharma's dependent origination is "dull" — such a person may even be very clever
quiz.why: "Their faculties are dull, clouded, and feeble." Venerable Miào Jìng: not believing in the Dharma's principle of dependent origination is what "dull" means — such a person may still be very intelligent.

quiz.q: What visible signs mark the pride-type?
options: restless, held-high faculties, delighting in adornment, speaking loudly, disliking humility
quiz.why: "Their faculties are restless, held high, and scattered; they delight in adorning the body, speak loudly and boastfully, and take no pleasure in humility." Master Cháng Bǎi: the pride-type holds the head high and cannot humbly bow to parents and teachers.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng view the discursive-type's "much confusion and doubt"?
options: doubt is also a mark of an intelligent person
quiz.why: "Their faculties are unsettled, flighty, agitated, and scattered." Venerable Miào Jìng: doubt, too, is a mark of the intelligent — the look of a wise person.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which can shift — the vow or the lineage?
options: the vow can shift and be abandoned; the lineage can never shift or be abandoned
quiz.why: "The vow itself may shift, may be abandoned — but the underlying lineage can never shift, can never be abandoned." Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the treatise's position — vows can shift, but one's original lineage cannot.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "lineage" is?
options: undefiled seeds in the storehouse consciousness — for a hearer, seeds of the hearer vehicle
quiz.why: "Precisely because their lineage is that of a hearer-disciple, they will in time inevitably abandon that vow and settle permanently into the hearer-disciple's vow alone." Venerable Miào Jìng: their storehouse consciousness holds undefiled seeds belonging to the hearer vehicle.
